nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite list of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, let $\varphi$ and $\psi$ be such formulas, and write $\varphi, \Gamma$ for the list $\Gamma$ with $\varphi$ added in front. If $\Gamma \vdash \varphi$ and $\varphi, \Gamma \vdash \psi$ in natural deduction, then $\Gamma \vdash \psi$.
nodes.title: Cut

nodes.summary: Fix a first-order language $L$ and a type $\alpha$ of variables; formulas and terms below are those of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$. For a formula $\varphi$ with one additional bound variable and a term $t$, write $\varphi[t]$ for $\varphi$ with $t$ substituted for that bound variable and $\forall \varphi$ for its universal quantification. Write $\neg \psi$ for $\psi \to \bot$, and $\psi, \Gamma$ for the…
nodes.title: Natural deduction

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite list of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, let $\varphi$ be such a formula with one additional bound variable, let $t$ be a term, and write $\varphi[t]$ for $\varphi$ with $t$ substituted for that bound variable. If $\Gamma \vdash \varphi[t]$ in natural deduction, then $\Gamma \vdash \exists \varphi$, where $\exists \varphi$ abbreviates…
nodes.title: Existential introduction

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory, that is, a set of sentences of a first-order language $L$, and regard each sentence of $T$ as a formula with free variables in $\alpha$. If a formula $\varphi$ with free variables in $\alpha$ is provable from these formulas, then $\varphi$ holds in every model of $T$ under every assignment of elements of the model to the variables in $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Soundness for theories

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, let $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be finite lists of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$ such that every member of $\Gamma$ is a member of $\Delta$, and let $\varphi$ be such a formula. If $\Gamma \vdash \varphi$ in natural deduction, then $\Delta \vdash \varphi$.
nodes.title: Weakening

nodes.summary: The empty context does not derive `⊥`.
nodes.title: Consistency of the calculus

nodes.summary: A set $T$ of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$ proves such a formula $\varphi$ when there is a finite list $\Gamma$ of members of $T$ with $\Gamma \vdash \varphi$ in natural deduction.
nodes.title: Provability from a set of formulas

For a formula $\psi$ of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, write $f(\psi)$ for Mathlib's relabeling of $\psi$ by $f$, which replaces each free variable $x$ by $f(x)$, and for a finite list $\Gamma$ of such formulas write $f(\Gamma)$ for the list obtained by applying this to each member of $\Gamma$. nodes.title: Injective relabeling preserves derivability

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon \alpha \to \beta$ be an injective map between types of variables. For a formula $\psi$ of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, write $f(\psi)$ for the renaming of the free variables of $\psi$ by $f$, and for a finite list $\Gamma$ of such formulas write $f(\Gamma)$ for the list obtained by renaming each member of $\Gamma$. If $\Gamma$ is such a list, $\varphi$ is such a formula…
nodes.title: Injective renaming preserves derivability

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite list of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, and let $\varphi$ be such a formula. If $\Gamma \vdash \varphi$ in natural deduction, then for every $L$-structure $M$ and every assignment $v \colon \alpha \to M$ under which all members of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds under $v$.
nodes.title: Soundness of first-order natural deduction

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a list of first-order formulas and let $s$ and $t$ be terms. If the equation $s = t$ is derivable from the hypotheses $\Gamma$, then the equation $t = s$ is derivable from $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Symmetry of equality in natural deduction

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a list of first-order formulas and let $r$, $s$ and $t$ be terms. If the equations $r = s$ and $s = t$ are both derivable from the hypotheses $\Gamma$, then the equation $r = t$ is derivable from $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Transitivity of equality in natural deduction

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
